questions.stem: Sales representatives must see only their own region's rows in a warehouse table. What do you build?

options.text: Dynamic data masking on the Region column
A view per region, shared by email
A security policy that applies an inline table-valued function as a filter predicate

questions.explanation: Row-level security uses a predicate function and a security policy, so every query on the table returns only the rows the predicate allows for the user.

questions.stem: Analysts may query a Patients table but must never read its Diagnosis column. Which T-SQL statement implements column-level security?

options.text: ALTER TABLE dbo.Patients DROP COLUMN Diagnosis
GRANT SELECT ON dbo.Patients (PatientID, Name, City) TO Analysts

questions.explanation: Granting SELECT on a list of columns lets the role read those columns only. A query that touches Diagnosis fails for them.

questions.stem: A reporting role must never read the dbo.StagingOrders table. Which statement implements object-level security?

options.text: DENY SELECT ON dbo.StagingOrders TO ReportingRole
ALTER TABLE dbo.StagingOrders DROP COLUMN ReportingRole
GRANT SELECT ON dbo.StagingOrders TO ReportingRole

questions.explanation: Object-level security controls access to whole objects such as tables and views with GRANT, REVOKE and DENY.

questions.stem: Users may read some folders in a lakehouse's Files section but not others. What controls access at folder level?

options.text: OneLake security roles that grant access to specific folders and tables

questions.explanation: OneLake security lets you define roles over specific tables and folders, so access to data is granted below the item level.
